title: introduce-session-shim-and-unify-stream-iterator-refresh-policy-across-sdks
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: We have several SDK mismatches around streaming session lifecycle and token refresh behavior that cause subtle consumer bugs (stale auth during long-lived streams, double-reconnects when resumed). This PR introduces a small compatibility shim (SessionShim) and a documented RefreshPolicy abstraction implemented in Python / TypeScript / Go SDKs to normalize behavior across languages. Summary: 1) Adds SessionShim: single, minimal surface that owns in-stream handshake, session metadata, and refresh token choreography. 2) Introduces RefreshPolicy interface and two bundled implementations (RefreshOn401 and ProactiveRefreshWithGrace) and a recommended default. 3) Unifies stream iterator semantics: generator/async-iterator (Python/TS) and channel semantics (Go) now expose the same resume() and checkpoint() helpers. 4) Adds per-SDK ergonomic helpers: with_session(), session_context(), and SessionClient to reduce boilerplate. 5) Small version bumps: python 1.14.0, typescript 0.28.1, go 0.38.0 (minor semver for ergonomics). 6) Test harness and integration tests that simulate long-running streams with intermittent credential rotation. Why a shim: We avoid breaking consumers by providing the new behaviors behind a small opt-in shim and a default that mirrors previous semantics for short-lived streams. Migration: consumers can opt into strict mode by enabling SessionShim in client config or by using the new with_session()/session_context() helpers. Files changed (high level): - sdk/python/redwood/session.py: new SessionShim, RefreshPolicy and helpers. - sdk/python/redwood/streaming_iter.py: iterator normalization and unit tests. - sdk/typescript/src/session.ts: SessionShim + types for RefreshPolicy and iterator helpers. - sdk/typescript/src/streaming/index.ts: iterator adaptors and examples. - sdk/go/session/shim.go: SessionShim and small channel adapter. - examples/long_running_streams/*: new examples showing token rotation. - docs/sdk-migration.md: migration notes and recommended config. Commits: - ae2f3b7: add python SessionShim and basic tests - b4d1c92: typescript RefreshPolicy infra and iterator adapters - c18d5e4: go shim + channel adapter and examples - d7f8a61: integration harness for credential rotation - e4c9b12: docs and migration guide Adjustments after review: - Reduced surface area of SessionClient after Priya flagged unnecessary methods; moved advanced helpers to experimental namespace. - Added a default ProactiveRefreshWithGrace with a 60s drift window to avoid 401 spikes during bursts (requested by Liam). - Fixed a race in the Go channel adapter that caused double-close on context cancel (Evan patch). Testing: - Unit tests added in each SDK for iterator resume/checkpoint behavior. - Integration test that rotates a short-lived token every 90s while maintaining a stream for 15 minutes; validated no silent disconnects. - Load test: 2k concurrent streams for 10 minutes in perf lab to validate memory usage. CI: initial runs failed due to flaky TS stream test; added 200ms jitter to helper in the harness and re-ran. All checks green at merge. Backwards compatibility: default clients behave identically for existing short-lived use-cases. Long-lived stream consumers are recommended to enable SessionShim or switch to the new with_session() helpers. Rollout: staged release - published python wheels and TS packages to npm beta channel for one week, Go module tag pushed and consumers notified. Notes for release engineers: tag python 1.14.0, typescript 0.28.1-beta -> promote after one week, go v0.38.0. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] docs - [x] examples - [x] changelog entry - [x] version bumps - [x] rollback strategy (disable SessionShim via client config) Related work: aligns with ENG-4321 (stream reliability) and ENG-4399 (cross-sdk parity for auth).
